PHP names anonymous classes with the prefix class@anonymous (or ParentName@anonymous if it extends a parent), followed by a NUL byte and the file path and offset.

In clean and onion architectures, source code dependencies point inward toward the domain at the center, so inner layers have no knowledge of outer layers.
Keeping domain entities free of framework and ORM imports (only PHP language and standard library) is a core principle of clean/hexagonal architecture.
Controllers and Twig templates belong to the presentation (UI/infrastructure) layer, not the business-logic layer; they merely invoke use cases that live in the application or domain layer.
In onion architecture, the domain model (entities and domain logic) forms the innermost core, with layers like application services and infrastructure surrounding it.
Tools like deptrac analyze class dependencies against configured layer rules and report or fail the build when a forbidden dependency exists.
In Clean Architecture, use cases should not depend on framework or infrastructure concerns like HTTP requests or EntityManager; they should receive plain input data and depend on abstractions.
A repository provides an in-memory-like collection interface for aggregates or entities while abstracting away the underlying persistence mechanism.

In clean architecture, the domain and use cases depend only on abstractions (ports/interfaces), so the database is an outer-layer detail that can be replaced by a new adapter without changing inner layers.

Value Objects are defined by their attribute values rather than a unique identity, and they are immutable, so equality is based on field values.

In Domain-Driven Design, repositories are defined per aggregate root, since the root is the only entry point for accessing and modifying objects within the aggregate.
In Domain-Driven Design, the ubiquitous language is the shared vocabulary used by developers and domain experts, derived from and reflected in the domain model.
The question describes the boundary within which a model and its language stay consistent, which is the context in which the words have their intended meaning.

DDD advocates a rich domain model where behavior and business rules live within entities and value objects, and the anemic model (getters/setters with logic in services) is widely considered an anti-pattern.
In Domain-Driven Design, a bounded context delimits where a particular model applies, so the same real-world concept (e.g., a Customer) can be modeled as different classes in different contexts.
The Symfony DI container instantiates a service only when it is first requested, unless it is explicitly marked as lazy-proxied or eagerly needed by another service.
The debug:router command (alias for debug:route in older versions) lists all registered routes in a Symfony application.
Symfony's autowiring and autoconfiguration let services be registered automatically via resource loading in services.yaml, so manual declaration of every service is not required.

PostgreSQL's MVCC means readers do not block writers and writers do not block readers, since readers see a consistent snapshot while writers create new row versions.

UPDATE and DELETE statements with WHERE clauses on indexed columns can locate matching rows faster via the index, just like SELECT.
ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT undoes only the statements executed after the named savepoint while keeping the rest of the transaction open.

HTTP 204 No Content indicates the request succeeded and there is no content to return in the response body.

XSS is prevented by context-aware output encoding/escaping when data is rendered, since input validation alone cannot stop all XSS and data may be safe in one context but not another.
The authorization server redirects to redirect_uri with a 'code' query parameter, which the client exchanges for an access token at the token endpoint.
Refresh tokens have a longer lifetime than access tokens and are used to obtain new access tokens without requiring the user to re-authenticate.
Salts are stored alongside the hash and are not secret; their purpose is to prevent precomputed rainbow table attacks, and verification uses the stored salt.

A PHPUnit data provider supplies multiple argument sets, and the test runs once for each set, not just one.
PHPUnit's expectException() method declares that the test expects an exception of the given class to be thrown.
It is reversed: a stub only returns canned data for method calls, while a mock additionally verifies that expected methods were called on it.
